messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The representation task involves mapping from normal and view directions to RGB values using a neural network (NN), as shown in Figure 3a." -- cites: E4 (Figure 3): observation "The first task simply reproduces a given appearance, i.e., it maps from normal and view directions to RGB values using a NN."
2. "The learning-to-learn task maps an image to a DAM representation, as depicted in Figure 3b." -- cites: E4 (Figure 3): observation "In a learning-to-learn task a network maps an image to a DAM representation."
3. "The learning-to-learn task aims to generalize appearance across different geometries, as indicated in Section 6." -- cites: E1 (Section 6): quote "Transfer of appearance captured from a real world image sequence to other complex geometry is shown in Fig. 12."

Cited evidence:
[E1] (text, Section 6, page 8): We have collected a second dataset of photographs of spherical objects with complex appearance (glossy objects under natural light). In particular we use 3 different materials and 5 different illuminations each with 5 images from registered views (Fig. 11 ) for training and 70 for testing. Please see the supplemental video for the animation. Transfer of appearance captured from a real world image sequence to other complex geometry is shown in Fig. 12 . Tbl. 2 summarizes the outcome for the representation task previously explored for synthetic data only. An example result is seen in Fig. 1 , more are shown in the supplemental materials. Our method can estimate view-dependent appearance, unlike RM/RM++, from a small training set, but it
[E4] (figure, Figure 3, page 4) (image attached): Figure 3. Different appearance processing tasks that we address using our deep appearance maps. a) The ﬁrst task simply reproduces a given appearance, i. e., it maps from normal and view directions to RGB values using a NN. b) In a learning-to-learn task a network maps an image to a DAM representation. c) Finally, in the segmentation-and-estimation task, a network maps an image to multiple DAMs and multiple segmentation networks. [image]

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E4 (Figure 3a) states that the first task simply reproduces a given appearance, i.e., it maps from normal and view directions to RGB values using a NN, which aligns with the claim.
The evidence in E4 (Figure 3b) shows that in a learning-to-learn task, a network maps an image to a DAM representation, which supports the claim.

The evidence in E1 (Section 6) discusses the transfer of appearance captured from a real-world image sequence to other complex geometries, but it does not specify that the learning-to-learn task aims to generalize appearance across different geometries. The claim goes beyond the evidence provided.
